venture.name: Zap Band
venture.business_concept: Proposed personal wearable alarm using adjustable electrical pulses to wake its wearer with less disturbance to other people.
venture.primary_product: Wearable wake-up alarm; wristband, patch, or another comfortable wearable form remains undecided.
venture.customer_need: Wake at a chosen time without a loud room-wide alarm.
venture.value_proposition: Quiet individual waking with simple controls, comfort, reliability, and affordability as design goals.
venture.geographic_market: Workspace says anywhere; Connecticut and New York are discussed as possible test markets.
venture.research_market_assumption: United States online retail in USD is the primary benchmark. UK TabTime is a separate comparable-market reference, without currency conversion.
venture.distribution_assumption: Direct-to-consumer online sales are a research assumption, not a confirmed venture decision.
venture.development_status: Concept; safety, waking effectiveness, reliability, and comfort are not established product claims.
venture.prior_research: Workspace reports 29 selected Amazon reviews and a simulation with three fictional participants. These are background hypotheses, not representative demand or willingness-to-pay evidence.
venture.source: User-provided venture workspace.pdf, all 10 pages visually reviewed; venture details on pages 1, 3, 7, 9 and 10.

competitors.name: Pavlok
competitors.geographic_market: US online store; international sales subject to destination terms
competitors.target_customers: Heavy sleepers and people seeking to change habits
competitors.main_products: Electrical-stimulus alarm wearables and habit tools
competitors.differentiating_features: Electrical stimulus, vibration, app control; MAX adds on-device screen controls
competitors.reason_for_inclusion: Closest mechanism and wearable form to the proposed Zap Band.

competitors.name: Google Fitbit
competitors.target_customers: Consumers seeking fitness and sleep tracking with a wrist alarm
competitors.main_products: Fitness trackers with vibrating Smart Wake alarms
competitors.differentiating_features: Combines a wrist alarm with activity and sleep tracking
competitors.reason_for_inclusion: A consumer can satisfy the quiet-wrist-alarm need while gaining broader tracking functions.

competitors.name: Sonic Alert
competitors.target_customers: Heavy sleepers, travelers, and people needing tactile alarm signals
competitors.main_products: Vibrating pillow and bed-shaker alarm clocks
competitors.differentiating_features: No wrist device required; physical alarm controls and vibration options
competitors.reason_for_inclusion: Offers a lower-cost tactile substitute; shared-bed vibration may still disturb a partner.

competitors.name: TabTime
competitors.geographic_market: UK storefront in GBP; US delivery and landed cost unverified
competitors.target_customers: People needing silent daily reminders or a personal wake-up alarm
competitors.differentiating_features: Ten daily vibration alarms, two-button controls, rechargeable battery
competitors.reason_for_inclusion: Relevant simple wrist-worn alternative, but vibration differs from electrical stimulus and the observed offer is UK-based.

comparison_groups.description: One representative hardware offer per US brand; broad tactile-waking substitutes, not feature-equivalent products.
Narrower wrist-wearable comparison; electrical stimulus versus vibration, only two brands.
All six researched USD hardware offers; multiple offers per brand, so not the headline competitor average.

pricing_model_comparison.one_time_purchase: All four brands have hardware purchase offers.
pricing_model_comparison.monthly_rental: Pavlok P03; $239.88 for 12 months of use, without ownership.
pricing_model_comparison.optional_subscriptions: Pavlok Plus P04 and P05 are software add-ons and excluded from hardware averages.
pricing_model_comparison.freemium_or_trial: Conditional three-month Google Health Premium offer; Pavlok rental is paid, not a free trial.
pricing_model_comparison.normalization: P03 x 12 = $239.88; P04 x 12 = $59.88; P05 / 12 = $2.4992 per month. These are separate recurring-cost illustrations.

market_opportunities.observation: The closest electrical-stimulus benchmark costs $159.99; selected vibration substitutes cost less.
market_opportunities.interpretation: A focused lower-price electrical wearable may appeal to students, but this is an opportunity hypothesis, not proof of an empty market.

market_opportunities.observation: Pavlok offers app control; MAX and TabTime show that on-device controls already exist.
market_opportunities.interpretation: Make reliable offline alarm operation and clear setup central to execution; do not claim those features are unique.

market_opportunities.observation: Workspace review themes include reliability and comfort, based on only 29 selected reviews.
market_opportunities.interpretation: Test overnight fit, battery alerts, alarm retention, and partner disturbance with real users before promising benefits.

market_opportunities.observation: Pavlok sells optional bands and upgrades; TabTime offers sizes and colors.
market_opportunities.interpretation: Consider optional washable or replaceable bands and a two-person bundle. Set any discount only after costs are known.

preliminary_pricing_recommendation.rationale: Test a focused alarm at $79–$99, below Shock Clock 3 and near or below Inspire 3. A premium over simple vibration substitutes requires demonstrated comfort, reliable waking, easy controls, and a credible returns policy.
preliminary_pricing_recommendation.position: 38.1%–50.6% below the $159.99 Shock Clock 3; $0.95–$20.95 below Inspire 3. Above the $35 Sonic Shaker. No GBP-to-USD comparison is made.
conditions: Test willingness to pay with real customers
Demonstrate safe operation and reliable waking
Include core alarm functions without a recurring fee

research_limitations: Research is a public-page snapshot checked on 2026-10-27. No checkout, order, stock reservation, or physical product test was performed.
Prices are listed device charges, not fully landed totals. Sales tax, shipping, duties, eligibility-based discounts, and optional accessories are excluded unless specified.
Four brands are a purposive competitor sample, not a census. Researched product ranges are selected-offer ranges, not complete catalogues.

Broad USD statistics compare one representative hardware offer per US brand for the tactile-waking need. Different mechanisms and features limit equivalence. Narrow wearable statistics use only Pavlok and Fitbit.
TabTime is a UK reference only. Its GBP price is not converted or included in US averages, and US availability is unverified.
Pavlok has conflicting reference-discount labels and older rental amounts. Live product selectors are used; promotional status and some terms need checkout confirmation.
Displayed regular/reference prices do not establish that those prices were historically charged. Fitbit search-result promotions were stale relative to the live product pages.
Manufacturer feature and battery statements are claims, not independent performance evidence. Zap Band safety, efficacy, comfort, and reliability remain design goals.
Distribution channel, final product form, production costs, return costs, demand, and willingness to pay are unknown. U.S. online retail is an explicit working assumption.
The supplied Amazon review summary is small and selected; synthetic focus-group responses are not real consumer demand. Neither establishes willingness to pay.
Google Health Premium is optional. Its page displayed From $9.99, but a billing interval and renewal total were not established in the retrieved page, so no complete priced plan is inferred.
